title: Deployment liaison — weekly digest: issues & decisions (2026-11-18)
body:
Weekly liaison digest — 2026-11-18

Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Marco Chen, Lena Gómez, Tomás Rivera, + SRE on-call (brief)
Slack: #onprem-ops, #install-field
Purpose: consolidate week’s install blockers, triage decisions, and handoff items for customer-facing on-prem/VPC installs. Focus this week on two recurring classes of issues: network path/mtu and credential/KMS rotations during initial handoff.

TL;DR:
- Acme Telecom: persistent gRPC stalls traced to MTU mismatch across customer NAT devices -> workaround identified (MSS clamping), mitigation tested on one node.
- Northbridge Health: KMS rotation failed during day-two validation due to missing AssumeRole policy for service account — rollback done, hotfix PR open.
- Canary upgrade (1.8.2 with quant-lib v0.9) saw NVLink driver incompatibility on older P4s; decision is to add driver check to canary gate and delay auto-upgrade for affected hosts.

Detailed notes:
1) Network path / MTU (Acme Telecom)
- Symptom: intermittent 50–400ms spikes in tail latency during large chat requests; correlates with windowed token bursts.
- Investigation: tcpdump and gRPC logs showed repeated retransmits and MSS fragmentation when payloads cross the customer-edge NAT. Intermediate device (vendor: NetEdge X) is clamping to 1400 while nodes use 1500 -> gRPC stalls under load.
- Temporary mitigation tested: enable MSS clamping on gateway, lower interface MTU on affected node pool, and add gRPC keepalive tuning (keepalive_time=60s).
- Decision: implement MSS clamp as first-line; create preflight check to detect MTU mismatch (preflight-mtu-check.sh).
- Owner: Marco Chen. Due: 2026-11-21. Ticket: JIRA:ONPREM-937.

2) KMS / credential handoff (Northbridge Health)
- Symptom: day-two validation failed at encryption key rotation step (rotation aborted, service degraded for ~10m).
- Root cause: customer’s IAM role used for KMS rotate lacked sts:AssumeRolePermission for the operator role (policy drift during admin re-org). Our deploy assumed rotation would be allowed by default.
- Action: applied emergency rollback to previous key, engaged customer infra team, and opened a small audit ticket for a post-ops runbook addition that includes a KMS permissions checklist. Hotfix PR created to catch missing policies at preflight.
- Owner: Lena Gómez (runbook update). Due: 2026-11-24. Linked ticket: JIRA:ENG-4821.

3) Canary upgrade failures (serving-runtime 1.8.2 + quant-lib v0.9)
- Observed failure mode: on nodes with Nvidia driver < 520.80, quant-lib emits illegal instructions causing process crash during kernel selection.
- Scope: affected 12% of dedicated pools in EU-west region (older P4s). Canary rolled back after 2 failures.
- Decision: update canary gating to include driver version check; block auto-upgrade until operator confirms driver >= 520.80 OR add soft-fallback to CPU path.
- Owner: Tomás Rivera (upgrade gating), with Engineering Runtime to provide fallback. Due: 2026-11-22. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1293

4) Observability gaps discovered during installs
- Missing metric: per-route KV-cache hit-rate during initial warmup — makes it hard to explain early cost spikes to customers.
- Short-term: add a per-deployment warmup dashboard tile (Console) and a short explanation for customers during handoff.
- Owner: Aisha Patel + Console team. Due: 2026-11-25.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we add MSS clamping to the standard network prescriptive for all on-prem installs? Pros: fewer late-stage surprises. Cons: invasive network change on some customer infra. Proposal: make it a recommended opt-in checkbox during site-preflight and escalate to opt-out only when customer refuses.
- How do we get timely driver inventory from customers? Current approach (agent.collect() during install) misses air-gapped sites. Consider an offline node-agent bundle that operators can run and upload.
- Add explicit KMS/AssumeRole examples to handoff checklist (sample trust policy snippet).

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco Chen — implement preflight-mtu-check.sh and enable MSS clamp runbook draft — 2026-11-21 — JIRA:ONPREM-937
- Lena Gómez — add KMS permission checklist to the day-two runbook + publish example trust policy — 2026-11-24 — JIRA:ENG-4821
- Tomás Rivera — change canary gating to include NV driver check; coordinate fallback path with runtime team — 2026-11-22 — PR #1293
- Aisha Patel / Console — add warmup dashboard tile + handoff blurb for customers — 2026-11-25
- SRE on-call — run expanded preflight on next three installs and report anomalies in #install-field — next three installs

Handoff notes for Customer Success (CS)
- Two customers impacted this week: Acme Telecom (MTU), Northbridge Health (KMS). CS play: delay final acceptance until we confirm preflight checks pass; offer a low-risk rollback window (24h) after rotation/upgrade.
- Communication template (short): explain root cause, steps we took (mitigation applied), next steps and expected date for final fix. Keep legal/compliance in loop for KMS incidents.

Quick links referenced above:
- Confluence playbook (edge prescriptive): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEPLOY-EDGE-STRAT
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1293
- Tickets: JIRA:ONPREM-937, JIRA:ENG-4821

Misc (brain dump)
- Might be worth a small cross-team sync (runtime + install + console) next Tue 2026-11-23 to sign off on gating and dashboard changes.
- Keep the preflight scripts minimal and auditable — customers dislike opaque changes.

If anything else surfaces overnight, I’ll append to this doc (notes-to-self style).

— Aisha
